title: Compare Exact Product Experiences
summary: Use dated first-party evidence to compare model endpoints, assistants, developer agents, frameworks, and managed agent services.
objectives: Compare exact experiences without ranking entire providers.
Use documented, tested, inference, and unknown evidence correctly.
Separate model capability from harness behavior within a provider family.
Apply observation and review dates to volatile claims.

sections.title: The comparison unit is the configured experience
paragraphs: Compare the surface a learner can actually use: model endpoint, consumer product, developer tool, framework application, managed service, or composed system. Record the version, date, tools, permissions, state, and runtime.
The same provider can supply both a model and an agentic product. Those are not contradictory classifications because they describe different boundaries.

Start by naming the exact experience. Then ask who generates output, who validates a proposed action, who executes it, who stores state, who supplies feedback, and who stops the run. If a value is unavailable, record UNKNOWN rather than borrowing a capability from another product bearing the same provider or model name.

This module uses a documentation-backed snapshot with asOf 2026-07-27 and reviewBy 2026-10-25. It is dated teaching evidence. It is not freshly verified as of the module's fixed audit date, 2026-09-19, and it does not establish behavior for an unobserved version, configuration, account, or run.
sections.callout: A provider is not the comparison unit. The unit is an exact, version-scoped product experience and configuration.

sections.title: Keep evidence kinds separate
paragraphs: Documented means a current first-party source directly describes a contract or behavior. Tested means a controlled run of the exact version and configuration produced retained evidence. Inference is a cited conclusion. Unknown is unresolved.
Documentation about a feature is not proof that a particular account, mode, or run used it. A live test does not establish future behavior after versions or configuration change.

The supplied casepack is documentation-only. It claims no live controlled execution. Its individual claims may be documented or inference, while unresolved details remain in unknowns. The structural auditor rejects a tested claim unless that claim includes nonempty runEvidence.

A structural audit can establish that required fields, dates, source bindings, family coverage, and pair relations are internally consistent. It cannot establish that the cited documentation is true, that a product still behaves as documented, or that a particular run succeeded.
sections.callout: Passing audit.py establishes structural consistency only. It is not a capability test or an independent verification of source truth.

sections.title: Use model-versus-harness pairs
paragraphs: Pairs make boundaries visible: Claude API and Claude Code; an OpenAI model and Codex; MAI model endpoints and Foundry Agent Service; Gemini API and an ADK application; Kimi or DeepSeek tool-call APIs and the client loops around them.
For xAI and consumer assistants, qualify the exact mode and enabled connectors. For open-weight deployments, separate access to model artifacts from the agent framework and executor.

The canonical casepack contains exactly eight provider families: anthropic, openai, microsoft, google, xai, moonshot-kimi, deepseek, and open-weight. Four explicit within-family relations pair a model role with a distinct harness role for Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google.

Transfer the method rather than a provider ranking. The Kimi records distinguish a model API from a conditional application-managed loop. The DeepSeek record distinguishes function-call proposals from user-code execution. The open-weight records distinguish a locally served model from a smolagents runtime. These cases show that the same responsibility questions apply beyond the largest hosted providers.
sections.callout: A valid pair has one provider family, two distinct case IDs, a model role, a harness role, and an explicit relation explaining the boundary.

sections.title: Volatile claims expire
paragraphs: Every product claim needs an observation date, review date, source owner, affected content, and a rule for downgrade or removal. Recheck sooner after a rename, runtime release, permission change, incident, or documentation revision.
When a source becomes stale or contradictory, block publication, preserve the old evidence for audit, and mark the current conclusion unknown until reviewed.

The auditor accepts an explicit --as-of date and defaults to the fixed teaching date 2026-09-19. If the casepack or any source or case has reviewBy earlier than that date, it prints STALE lines, prints BLOCKED, and exits unsuccessfully. It never turns stale evidence into an unconditional pass.

Do not silently replace the supplied dates. Reverification requires reviewing the exact source and, where a runtime claim is needed, retaining controlled run evidence for the exact version, configuration, permissions, tools, and user journey.
sections.callout: Freshness is part of a claim. Historical evidence remains auditable even when current publication is blocked.

sections.title: Worked case: Claude model endpoint versus Claude Code
paragraphs: Begin with anthropic-claude-api-model, Claude through the Messages API. Its conclusionClass is model. The documented request creates model messages from supplied messages, model configuration, and optional tools. Its boundary records goalDirectedRun absent, toolAccess external, state application-managed, and feedbackLoop application-managed.

Decision trace for the model row: the model can generate output and may propose a tool use, but the cited endpoint is not identified as the authorized tool executor, durable state owner, or loop controller. Therefore the exact endpoint is classified as a model component. Unknowns retain the untested model version, account configuration, tool schema, and client loop.

Now examine anthropic-claude-code. Its conclusionClass is agentic-system. The cited Claude Code description documents a repeated gather-context, take-action, and verify-results loop. Its case records goalDirectedRun, modelDirectedNextStep, toolAccess, externalSideEffects, and feedbackLoop as present, with product-managed state and human control.

Decision trace for the harness row: the exact product experience adds context gathering, tool invocation, environmental effects, result feedback, verification, permissions, and repetition toward the user's coding goal. Therefore the configured Claude Code experience is classified as an agentic system.

The comparison does not classify Anthropic as a whole. It does not claim that every Claude surface is agentic or that every Claude Code run has identical authority. Permissions, sandboxing, interruption, repository scope, network access, enabled tools, and verification remain configuration-dependent responsibility boundaries.
sections.callout: Changing the comparison unit changes the supported conclusion. A tool-call proposal is not the same thing as authorized execution.

sections.title: Canonical dated casepack
paragraphs: Save the following artifact as casepack.json. It contains the full 14-case canonical evidence snapshot, the canonical source index, claim metadata, explicit unknowns, and four explicit model-versus-harness relations.

The source index contains 16 primary first-party records because that is the number present in the supplied canonical snapshot. The case count is 14. No generic source aliases, invented transfer cases, or placeholder capability rows are used.
The added pairs array makes the four required within-family relations machine-checkable without guessing from case ID suffixes. It does not alter any of the 14 canonical case records.
sections.callout: The casepack is as of 2026-07-27. Do not describe it as newly verified on 2026-09-19.

sections.title: Offline structural audit
paragraphs: Save the following program as audit.py in the same directory as casepack.json. It uses only the Python standard library and calls json.load on the supplied file. Editing casepack.json therefore changes the audit result. The relevant standard-library contracts are documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html, https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html#copy.deepcopy, https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date.fromisoformat, https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.parse.html#urllib.parse.urlparse, https://docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html, and https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.exit.

The validator checks root, source, case, claim, and pair shapes before set membership or hashing. It checks exact family coverage, duplicate IDs, nonempty owners, canonical YYYY-MM-DD dates, date order, freshness, future-dated root and source records, HTTPS source URLs, source ownership, evidence kinds, conclusion statuses, tested run evidence, and explicit pair roles. URL parsing errors are converted into controlled validation errors.

Each public negative test deep-copies the complete loaded fixture, changes one field, and expects one named reason. A separate silent assertion suite covers the recorded malformed-boundary issues, unique pair identities, future dates, controlled CLI behavior, and input immutability. The original loaded object is not mutated. The public negative-test stdout remains unchanged.

Run python3 audit.py for the fixed default date. Run python3 audit.py --as-of 2026-10-26 to demonstrate stale blocking. No execution of either command is claimed in this module. If you cannot run Python, record execution as UNKNOWN rather than claiming a pass.
sections.callout: The auditor validates the rendered file, but structural source binding cannot prove the truth or present-day accuracy of a claim.

sections.title: Independent changed-input challenge
paragraphs: Complete this task before reading the key. Create a deep copy of casepack.json and change exactly one field: in the source record anthropic-claude-code-loop, change reviewBy from 2026-10-25 to 2026-09-18. Run the auditor with --as-of 2026-09-19. Record the affected source, affected claims, historical evidence disposition, current conclusion disposition, owner, and next verification requirement.

Your answer must compare the full responsibility boundary for anthropic-claude-api-model and anthropic-claude-code. Cover generation, goal-directed control, tool proposal, tool execution, authority, state, feedback, external side effects, verification, stopping, and human control. Do not replace the exact-experience comparison with a provider-wide label.

Key: the changed source is anthropic-claude-code-loop. The affected Claude Code claims are claude-code-loop and claude-code-harness-boundary. The auditor prints STALE source anthropic-claude-code-loop reviewBy=2026-09-18 and blocks publication. Preserve the original dated evidence. Treat the current affected Claude Code conclusion as UNKNOWN pending review, assign provider-anthropic, and verify the exact source, version, configuration, permissions, tools, and user journey before issuing a new dated conclusion.

Boundary key: the Messages API row generates model output and may propose a next step, while execution, authorization, state, feedback, side effects, and continuation remain external or application-managed. The Claude Code row documents a goal-directed product loop with tool access, side effects, product-managed state, feedback, verification, and human control. Staleness removes confidence in the current harness conclusion, but it does not transform the model endpoint into an agent or erase the historical record.

Provider-neutral transfer: repeat the same analysis with open-weight-model-alone and open-weight-smolagents-system. The model alone does not inherit the framework's loop, memory, tools, executor, limits, or coordination. A passing structural audit still does not prove safe execution, correct tool results, or current runtime behavior.
sections.callout: Trace the changed field to affected claims and responsibilities. Preserve history, block publication, and use UNKNOWN until review.

activity.title: Build a dated cross-provider comparison
instructions: Select at least eight exact experiences spanning the eight provider families in the evidence matrix.
Include at least four within-family model-versus-harness comparisons.
Record observable behavior, classification, claim evidence kind, source, observation date, review date, boundaries, and unknowns.
Have another learner challenge one conclusion and revise or defend it using evidence.
Save the supplied casepack.json and audit.py, run the structural audit offline, and retain its stdout. If you cannot run Python, record execution as UNKNOWN rather than claiming a pass.

Complete the changed-input challenge independently before consulting its key. Compare generation, execution, authority, state, feedback, side effects, verification, stopping, and human responsibility.
Do not rank providers or infer capabilities for an unlisted product. Apply the responsibility-boundary method to new providers only after obtaining dated evidence for the exact experience.
evidence: A dated eight-family comparison with no provider-wide classification.
A retained challenge and disposition showing how contradictory or missing evidence was handled.
Four explicit within-family relations with distinct model and harness roles.
The unchanged full casepack, auditor, and retained output or an explicit UNKNOWN execution status.
A responsibility-boundary comparison and a provider-neutral transfer beyond Anthropic, OpenAI, and Microsoft.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which classification changed when you narrowed the unit from provider to exact experience?

cues.text: Begin by freezing the unit of comparison. We are not comparing logos, broad model families, or marketing categories. We are comparing an exact experience that a person or application can use. Ask learners to name the endpoint, application, developer tool, framework, managed service, or composed system. Then ask for the version if known, the configuration, enabled tools, permissions, state owner, runtime, observation date, and stopping behavior. If any of those facts are unavailable, the right entry is UNKNOWN. Do not import a capability from a neighboring product simply because it has the same provider or model name. A model can generate a proposed function call while a separate client validates arguments, authorizes access, executes code, records state, returns observations, and decides whether another turn occurs. Those responsibilities determine the boundary. Emphasize that this module uses a snapshot dated 2026-07-27 with review due 2026-10-25. It was not freshly browsed or retested on the fixed teaching date 2026-09-19. Ask learners to point to the component that generates output and then separately identify the component responsible for real-world effects.
Show model-versus-harness pairs across provider families without ranking them.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A text table lists provider family, exact model surface, exact agent or harness surface, observable distinction, evidence kind, and unknowns. Reduced-motion mode shows the complete table.

cues.text: Introduce the four evidence kinds one at a time. Documented means that a cited first-party source describes a contract or behavior. It does not prove that every account has the feature or that a particular run used it. Tested means a controlled run of the exact version and configuration produced retained evidence. A statement cannot become tested merely because someone expects it to work. Inference is a conclusion drawn from cited observations, such as concluding that an endpoint is not a complete agent because the client owns execution and loop continuation. Unknown means the available evidence does not resolve the question. The casepack is explicitly documentation-only, so it contains no claimed live controlled execution. Also distinguish claim kind from conclusion status. Claims may be documented, tested, inference, or unknown. Case conclusions use documented, qualified, or inference. Explain the auditor's limited scope. It can detect a missing source ID, malformed shape, cross-family source binding, or unsupported tested label. It cannot inspect vendor systems, establish that documentation is true, or verify that behavior remains current. Ask learners to rewrite the phrase 'the model uses tools' as two statements: the model may propose a tool call, and an identified runtime may validate and execute it.

Walk through the four explicit within-family pairs. Anthropic pairs Claude through the Messages API with Claude Code. OpenAI pairs an API model with Codex. Microsoft pairs the MAI image model endpoint with Foundry Agent Service. Google pairs a Gemini API model with an ADK agent application. In each pair, the left member has a model role and the right member has a distinct harness role. The relation text explains what the harness adds, so the auditor does not guess from an ID suffix. Then transfer the questions to the other families. Grok is qualified as an assistant because modes and connectors vary. Kimi's API model is separated from an application-managed loop. DeepSeek's official tool-call guide places function execution in user code. A locally served open-weight model remains a model, while smolagents can provide repeated model-and-tool steps, memory, limits, and managed-agent coordination. None of these observations ranks providers. They locate responsibility. Ask learners to identify who owns tool execution, state, feedback, authorization, budgets, recovery, terminal evidence, and human approval in one pair. Remind them that access to a tool-call syntax is not evidence that the model itself executes the tool.

Treat dates as part of every claim. The snapshot records an as-of date, review date, source owners, case owners, and individual observation dates. The fixed audit date is 2026-09-19. On that date the 2026-10-25 review deadline has not passed, but this still does not make the material newly verified on September nineteenth. Explain what happens when the explicit audit date moves beyond the review deadline. The program prints each stale root, source, and case item, prints BLOCKED, and exits unsuccessfully. It does not print an unconditional pass. A publication workflow should preserve the old record for audit, identify affected claims, assign the owner, and mark the current conclusion UNKNOWN until review. Contradiction also requires a scoped response. Do not delete the historical evidence, and do not relabel a contradiction as a successful test. Ask learners what would establish a new current claim. The answer is dated review of the exact source and, when runtime behavior matters, a controlled test of the exact version, configuration, permissions, tools, and user journey with retained run evidence. Recheck sooner after renames, releases, permission changes, incidents, and material documentation revisions.

Ask: If --as-of is 2026-10-26 and every reviewBy value is 2026-10-25, may the program print PASS? Expected answer: no. It must list stale items, print BLOCKED, and return failure. Ask what happens to historical evidence. Expected answer: retain it for audit while the affected current claim becomes UNKNOWN pending review.

Work the Anthropic comparison slowly and trace every decision. For anthropic-claude-api-model, the exact experience is Claude through the Messages API. The source documents message generation from supplied inputs and optional tools. The case records no goal-directed run at the endpoint boundary. Tool access and external side effects are external, while state, feedback, and human control are application-managed. The inference is scoped: because another component owns execution, authorization, state, and continuation, this endpoint alone is a model component rather than a complete agentic system. Now switch the comparison unit to anthropic-claude-code. The cited product description identifies a repeating cycle that gathers context, takes action, verifies results, and uses observations in later decisions. Its observable fields record goal-directed control, model-directed next steps, tool access, side effects, feedback, and human control as present, with product-managed state. That supports an agentic-system conclusion for the configured Claude Code experience. Stress what the comparison does not prove. It does not classify the provider, every Claude chat, or every Claude Code configuration. A particular run's authority depends on sandboxing, repository scope, network policy, approvals, enabled tools, interruption, and verification. Have learners state the changed unit and the exact responsibilities that changed.

Orient learners to the casepack before they copy it. The root records schema version, dates, owner, scope, evidence policy, taxonomy, source index, explicit pairs, and cases. There are fourteen case records and sixteen source records in the supplied canonical snapshot. The distinction matters because case count and source count are not interchangeable. Each source has an HTTPS URL, publisher, verification date, review date, owner, and primary trust tier. Each case has an exact experience, surface, owner, conclusion, observable behavior, claims, boundary notes, and unknowns. Point out that Kimi, DeepSeek, and open-weight claims bind to their own first-party source IDs rather than generic aliases. The four pair objects state one family, one model ID, one harness ID, and a nonempty relation. Explain that the pairs array is machine-checkable teaching metadata. It prevents a test from claiming pair coverage merely because two unrelated rows happen to exist. Invite learners to find one inference claim and explain why its source still matters. Then find an unknown and state what evidence would resolve it. Remind learners not to edit dates merely to make an audit pass.

Demonstrate the offline exercise as a code-reading practice even if Python cannot be run. The program opens the path supplied on the command line, defaults to casepack.json, and calls json.load. Therefore the rendered file is the data under audit. It does not substitute hardcoded rows. Shape checks occur before membership operations, so a None row, malformed source index, non-list sourceIds, or non-string element produces a controlled reason instead of an incidental traceback. The validator checks exact family equality, not merely a count of eight. It verifies duplicate IDs, owners, date order, HTTPS URLs, statuses, evidence kinds, direct source binding, source ownership, tested run evidence, and pair roles. Each negative test begins with copy.deepcopy of the full valid fixture and mutates one field. The expected reason must occur in the error list. This design prevents a shrunken fixture from passing a negative test only because unrelated coverage checks failed. Ask learners to predict the result of changing an Anthropic claim to use openai-models. The expected reason is cross-family-source. Finally repeat the responsibility boundary: structural consistency does not establish truth, live availability, safe execution, or successful outcomes.

Read the expected output as a deterministic specification rather than evidence of an actual run. On the default date, the first line names the snapshot and audit dates. Ten negative tests then report their expected specific reasons. The final line reports fourteen cases, sixteen sources, eight families, and four valid pairs. Explain that a learner's output should match only if the copied files are unchanged and the Python implementation follows standard behavior. The stale-date example is deliberately different. With an as-of date of 2026-10-26, the root, all sixteen sources, and all fourteen cases are stale because their review date is 2026-10-25. That is one plus sixteen plus fourteen, for thirty-one stale items. The last line is BLOCKED stale-items=31. The negative-test suite is not run after stale blocking because publication is already blocked. Ask learners why suppressing an unconditional pass matters. The answer is that a structurally complete record can still be outside its review window. If learners cannot execute the program, they must label execution UNKNOWN and may still inspect the deterministic logic and expected output.

Give learners the changed-input challenge without showing the key. They must deep-copy the casepack and change only the reviewBy field of anthropic-claude-code-loop to 2026-09-18. With an audit date of 2026-09-19, that source is stale. Require a trace containing the source ID, affected claim IDs, historical disposition, current conclusion, owner, and next verification action. Then require a full responsibility comparison. The Messages API row generates output and may propose calls, but the application owns validation, execution, authority, state, feedback, side effects, and continuation. Claude Code's documented harness adds a goal-directed loop, tool use, state, effects, verification, stopping behavior, and human control, subject to configuration. When its central source is stale, learners must not silently keep a current agentic-system claim. They preserve the old record and mark the affected current conclusion UNKNOWN pending review by provider-anthropic. For transfer, compare a locally served open-weight model with smolagents. The same model-versus-harness distinction applies without relying on a large hosted provider. Finish by reminding learners that neither the changed date nor the audit proves any product claim false. It proves that the evidence is outside the selected publication window.

Guide the eight-family comparison and peer challenge. Require exact experiences, all four explicit pairs, direct source IDs, unknowns, dates, owners, and a responsibility-boundary table. Allow time to copy the two artifacts, inspect or run the audit, complete the changed-input trace independently, compare with the key, and revise one conclusion. If execution is unavailable, require the learner to write UNKNOWN rather than report a fabricated pass.

Begin the knowledge check after the learner can compare exact experiences without ranking providers, distinguish documented from tested evidence, explain model and harness responsibilities, and block a stale claim while preserving its audit history.
